web_evidence.title: Goodbye Mr Chips by James Hilton
web_evidence.note: The complete 18-chapter digital-library text consistently narrates Chips externally as 'he' from the opening through his death and aftermath, while entering his memories through free-indirect thought; first-person passages are attributed speech or thought, not an alternating base narrator.

web_evidence.title: Goodbye Mr Chips Summary and Study Guide
web_evidence.note: The guide explicitly identifies the novel's narration as third-person limited omniscient and says it remains with Mr. Chips's thoughts and memories.

web_evidence.title: James Hilton | Good-bye Mr Chips | Slightly Foxed literary review
web_evidence.note: The literary review describes the novella as a bird's-eye view of Chips's whole career organized through his retrospection and reproduces third-person rendering of his views, corroborating the book-wide Chips-centered narrative structure.

search_log: Searched "Good-bye, Mr. Chips" "James Hilton" with excerpt, first-chapter, narrator, point-of-view, third-person, epistolary, frame, multiple-narrator, and alternating-narration terms.
Opened and inspected the complete Project Gutenberg Australia text at the opening, multiple interior chapter transitions, and Chapter 18; no sustained first- or second-person base section was found.
Opened SuperSummary's study guide, which explicitly describes third-person limited omniscient narration across the novel.
Opened the Slightly Foxed literary review for its whole-career structural description and corroborating passage.
Checked Open Library records and the 1934 Little, Brown edition listing; these verified the work and exposed only a short opening excerpt, so they were not relied upon for whole-book person.
Checked Hachette UK's publisher page; it advertised an excerpt but exposed only catalog copy in the accessible page, so its synopsis grammar was not treated as person evidence.
Targeted scholarly and publisher searches produced no stronger accessible structural analysis; irrelevant film, classroom-note, and snippet results were discarded.
person_note: The controlling narrator is nonparticipating and consistently refers to Mr. Chips in the third person while closely focalizing his memories, judgments, and free-indirect thoughts. The Goodreads quotations repeatedly exhibit that structure, and the complete web text confirms it from Chapter 1 through the final chapter without a change of base person. Apparent first person belongs to dialogue or quoted thought, while generic or locally addressed 'you' passages are gnomic reflection, free indirect discourse, or character address rather than second-person narration. The full-text evidence and explicit whole-book POV description agree; no material uncertainty or alternating frame remains.
